title: 2001 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 5
statement: What is the area of a square inscribed in a semicircle of radius 1 , with one of its sides flush with the diameter of the semicircle?

solutions.text: Call the center of the semicircle \(O\), a point of contact of the square and the circular part of the semicircle \(A\), the closer vertex of the square on the diameter \(B\), and the side length of the square \(x\). We know \(O A=1, A B=x, O B=\frac{x}{2}\), and \(\angle A B O\) is right. By the Pythagorean theorem, \(x^{2}=\frac{4}{5}\).
